questions.question: Which AWS service provides the ability to manage infrastructure as code?

explanation.summary: AWS CodePipeline is a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) service, not an infrastructure as code service.
explanation.why: AWS CodePipeline automates the steps required to release software changes such as source, build, test, and deploy phases. It does not define, provision, or manage infrastructure resources like servers, networks, or storage using templates. Infrastructure as code focuses on declaratively defining infrastructure state, which CodePipeline does not do. CodePipeline may orchestrate deployments that include IaC tools, but it is not itself an IaC service.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Introduction Devops Aws Continuous Integration

explanation.summary: AWS CodeDeploy is a deployment service and does not manage infrastructure definitions.
explanation.why: AWS CodeDeploy focuses on automating application deployments to EC2 instances, Lambda functions, or on-premises servers. It manages how application code is deployed, not how infrastructure resources are created or defined. Infrastructure as code requires declarative templates to create and manage resources, which CodeDeploy does not provide.

explanation.summary: AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity and is unrelated to infrastructure as code.
explanation.why: AWS Direct Connect establishes a private, dedicated network connection between on-premises environments and AWS. It is a networking service and does not define, provision, or manage AWS resources through code or templates.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudFormation enables infrastructure as code by allowing users to define and provision AWS resources using templates.
keyPoints: Uses declarative templates written in JSON or YAML
Automates provisioning and updating of AWS resources
Ensures infrastructure is consistent and repeatable
Manages dependencies between AWS resources automatically
Supports version control and change tracking
examples: Creating EC2 instances, VPCs, and security groups using a single template
Reproducing identical environments for development, testing, and production
Rolling back infrastructure automatically if a stack update fails
explanation.additionalInfo: Infrastructure as code is a core DevOps practice that treats infrastructure configuration the same way as application code. AWS CloudFormation allows teams to define the desired state of infrastructure in templates and lets AWS handle resource creation, updates, and deletion in the correct order. CloudFormation stacks provide lifecycle management, drift detection, and rollback capabilities, which are critical for safe and auditable infrastructure changes. Using CloudFormation reduces configuration drift, improves compliance, and enables automation at scale.

questions.question: According to security best practices, how should an Amazon EC2 instance be given access to an Amazon S3 bucket?

options.text: Hard code an IAM user's secret key and access key directly in the application, and upload the file.

explanation.summary: Hard coding credentials is a security anti-pattern and violates AWS best practices.
explanation.why: Embedding access keys in application code exposes credentials to source code leaks, reverse engineering, and accidental disclosure. Rotating credentials becomes difficult and compromised keys can be misused without detection. AWS explicitly advises against hard coding credentials in any application or script.

options.text: Store the IAM user's secret key and access key in a text file on the EC2 instance, read the keys, then upload the file.

explanation.summary: Storing credentials on an EC2 instance is insecure and discouraged.
explanation.why: Credentials stored on disk can be accessed by anyone who gains access to the instance. They are difficult to rotate and increase the blast radius of a security compromise. AWS provides role-based access to avoid storing long-term credentials entirely.

learnMore.title: Iam Id Roles Use Switch Role

options.text: Have the EC2 instance assume a role to obtain the privileges to upload the file.

explanation.summary: Using an IAM role attached to the EC2 instance is the recommended and secure method.
keyPoints: Eliminates the need for long-term credentials
Permissions are controlled using IAM policies
Follows the principle of least privilege
examples: An EC2 instance uploads logs to an S3 bucket using an attached IAM role
Applications access AWS services without storing credentials
Roles are updated without changing application code
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM roles for EC2 provide temporary credentials through the instance metadata service. These credentials are automatically managed by AWS and rotated frequently. This approach greatly reduces security risks compared to static credentials and simplifies credential management. It is a core requirement for secure production workloads and is heavily emphasized in AWS exams.

learnMore.title: Iam Id Roles Use Switch Role

options.text: Modify the S3 bucket policy so that any service can upload to it at any time.

explanation.summary: Allowing unrestricted access to an S3 bucket is insecure and violates security best practices.
explanation.why: Granting open access removes all access control and exposes the bucket to unauthorized uploads, data poisoning, and potential abuse. AWS security best practices require restricting access using IAM roles and policies, not broad public permissions.

questions.question: An online gaming company needs to choose a purchasing option to run its Amazon EC2 instances for 1 year. The web traffic is consistent, and any increases in traffic are predictable. The EC2 instances must be online and available without any disruption. Which EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

explanation.summary: On-Demand Instances provide flexibility but are not the most cost-effective for long-term, predictable workloads.
explanation.why: On-Demand pricing is ideal for short-term or unpredictable usage. For a 1-year, steady workload, paying the full On-Demand rate results in higher costs compared to commitment-based pricing options.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances provide the best cost savings for predictable, long-term workloads.
keyPoints: Up to 72 percent discount compared to On-Demand
examples: Gaming servers running continuously for a year
Production application servers with stable load
Backend services with predictable usage patterns
explanation.additionalInfo: Reserved Instances are designed for workloads with known and predictable usage. By committing to a 1-year term, customers receive significant discounts while maintaining guaranteed capacity and availability. Unlike Spot Instances, Reserved Instances are never interrupted by AWS. This makes them ideal for production systems such as online gaming platforms where uptime and performance are critical.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances are cost-effective but can be interrupted and are unsuitable for uninterrupted workloads.
explanation.why: Spot Instances can be terminated with little notice when AWS needs capacity back. This makes them inappropriate for workloads that must remain online without disruption, such as online gaming servers.

explanation.summary: Spot Fleet manages Spot Instances but does not eliminate interruption risk.
explanation.why: Spot Fleet helps optimize Spot Instance usage but still relies on Spot capacity, which can be reclaimed by AWS. It does not guarantee uninterrupted availability required for this scenario.

questions.question: Which option is a customer responsibility when using Amazon DynamoDB under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

explanation.summary: Physical security of DynamoDB is the responsibility of AWS, not the customer.
explanation.why: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which includes physical data center security, hardware, facilities, and infrastructure. Customers never manage or access the physical DynamoDB infrastructure.

explanation.summary: Patching DynamoDB is fully managed by AWS.
explanation.why: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed service. AWS handles operating system maintenance, software patching, updates, and availability. Customers do not control or perform any patching activities for DynamoDB.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for controlling access to DynamoDB tables using IAM and resource policies.
keyPoints: Customers manage IAM users, roles, and policies
Access is controlled through fine-grained permissions
Table access can be restricted by action and resource
Security configuration is owned by the customer
Misconfigured access can lead to data exposure
examples: Granting an IAM role permission to read from a specific table
Restricting write access to production tables
Using IAM conditions to limit access by IP or VPC
explanation.additionalInfo: In the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, customers are responsible for security in the cloud. For DynamoDB, this includes defining who can access tables, what actions they can perform, and under what conditions. AWS provides the tools such as IAM, resource-based policies, and encryption, but customers must configure them correctly. Improper access control is a common cause of security incidents and is frequently tested in AWS exams.

options.text: Encryption of data at rest in DynamoDB

explanation.summary: Encryption at rest in DynamoDB is handled by AWS by default.
explanation.why: Amazon DynamoDB automatically encrypts all data at rest using AWS-owned keys unless customer-managed keys are explicitly configured. The encryption mechanism itself is part of AWS's responsibility.

questions.question: Which option is a perspective that includes foundational capabilities of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)?

explanation.summary: Sustainability is a pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, not a CAF perspective.
explanation.why: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework defines six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations. Sustainability belongs to the Well-Architected Framework, making this option incorrect.

explanation.summary: Performance efficiency is a Well-Architected Framework pillar, not a CAF perspective.
explanation.why: AWS CAF focuses on organizational and operational readiness for cloud adoption, while performance efficiency is evaluated within the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

explanation.summary: Governance is one of the six core perspectives of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework.
keyPoints: Defines how cloud investments are governed
Focuses on risk management and compliance
examples: Defining account structures and guardrails
Implementing cost controls and budgets
Establishing compliance and audit processes
explanation.additionalInfo: The Governance perspective of AWS CAF ensures that cloud initiatives align with business goals while managing risk effectively. It covers areas such as financial management, portfolio management, compliance, and risk controls. Governance is foundational because it sets the rules and boundaries for cloud adoption, enabling organizations to scale securely and responsibly.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Governance Perspective Governance

explanation.summary: Reliability is a pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, not a CAF perspective.
explanation.why: AWS CAF and AWS Well-Architected Framework serve different purposes. Reliability belongs to Well-Architected and evaluates workload design, not organizational cloud adoption readiness.

questions.question: A company is running and managing its own Docker environment on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants an alternative to help manage cluster size, scheduling, and environment maintenance. Which AWS service meets these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service and does not manage container clusters.
explanation.why: Lambda runs individual functions without managing servers or containers directly. It does not provide cluster orchestration, scheduling, or container lifecycle management required for Docker environments.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service, not a container orchestration solution.
explanation.why: RDS manages databases such as MySQL and PostgreSQL. It does not handle container scheduling, cluster scaling, or Docker environment management.

explanation.summary: AWS Fargate removes the need to manage servers and clusters for containerized workloads.
keyPoints: Integrated with Amazon ECS and EKS
examples: Running Docker containers without managing EC2 instances
Automatically scaling container workloads
Deploying microservices using ECS with Fargate
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Fargate allows customers to focus entirely on application logic while AWS manages the underlying compute infrastructure. It handles cluster size, scheduling, and maintenance automatically. This makes it an ideal alternative for teams that want to move away from managing their own Docker clusters on EC2 while retaining container-based architectures.

explanation.summary: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service for data stored in Amazon S3.
explanation.why: Athena is used for querying data using SQL and does not manage containers, clusters, or compute scheduling.

questions.question: A company wants to run a NoSQL database on Amazon EC2 instances. Which task is the responsibility of AWS in this scenario?

options.text: Update the guest operating system of the EC2 instances.

explanation.summary: Updating the guest operating system on EC2 instances is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: When running workloads on Amazon EC2, customers are responsible for managing the guest operating system, including patching, updates, and configuration. AWS does not access or manage the OS inside customer instances.

options.text: Maintain high availability at the database layer.

explanation.summary: High availability at the database layer is the customer's responsibility when running databases on EC2.
explanation.why: When customers deploy their own databases on EC2, they must design and manage replication, backups, failover, and clustering. AWS only provides the underlying infrastructure, not database-level availability for self-managed databases.

options.text: Patch the physical infrastructure that hosts the EC2 instances.

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for patching and maintaining the physical infrastructure that runs EC2 instances.
keyPoints: AWS manages physical servers and data centers
Hardware maintenance is handled by AWS
Part of security of the cloud
examples: Replacing failed disks in EC2 host machines
Applying firmware updates to physical servers
Maintaining power, cooling, and networking hardware
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which includes physical data centers, servers, networking equipment, and hardware maintenance. Even when customers run fully self-managed databases on EC2, AWS continues to manage and patch the underlying physical infrastructure without customer involvement.

explanation.summary: Configuring security groups is the customer's responsibility.
explanation.why: Security groups act as virtual firewalls for EC2 instances. Customers define inbound and outbound rules to control traffic. AWS provides the security group feature, but customers are responsible for configuring it correctly.

questions.question: Which AWS services or tools can identify rightsizing opportunities for Amazon EC2 instances? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: AWS Cost Explorer helps identify cost trends and rightsizing opportunities for EC2 instances.
examples: Identifying EC2 instances with low CPU utilization
Reviewing cost trends to downsize overprovisioned instances
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Cost Explorer analyzes usage patterns and cost data to help customers understand where they can reduce spending. Its rightsizing recommendations are commonly used to identify EC2 instances that are over- or under-provisioned, making it a key exam answer for cost optimization scenarios.

learnMore.title: Aws Cost Management Aws Cost Explorer

explanation.summary: AWS Billing Conductor focuses on cost allocation and billing visibility, not rightsizing.
explanation.why: Billing Conductor helps manage and allocate costs across accounts and teams but does not analyze resource utilization or provide rightsizing recommendations.

explanation.summary: Amazon CodeGuru analyzes application code, not EC2 instance sizing.
explanation.why: CodeGuru focuses on code reviews and application performance profiling. It does not evaluate infrastructure utilization or recommend EC2 instance size changes.

explanation.summary: Amazon SageMaker is a machine learning service and does not provide EC2 rightsizing recommendations.
explanation.why: SageMaker is used to build, train, and deploy machine learning models. It does not analyze EC2 utilization for cost optimization purposes.

explanation.summary: AWS Compute Optimizer provides detailed rightsizing recommendations based on utilization metrics.
keyPoints: Analyzes CPU, memory, and network utilization
examples: Recommending a smaller EC2 instance for underutilized workloads
Suggesting instance family changes based on usage
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Compute Optimizer uses historical utilization metrics and machine learning to recommend optimal resource configurations. It is specifically designed for rightsizing EC2 instances and is frequently paired with AWS Cost Explorer in exam questions.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Trusted Advisor? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: AWS Trusted Advisor does not provide container orchestration.
explanation.why: Container orchestration is handled by services like Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS. Trusted Advisor focuses on best practice checks, not workload orchestration.

explanation.summary: Encryption key management is handled by AWS KMS, not Trusted Advisor.
explanation.why: Trusted Advisor may report on security posture but does not create or rotate encryption keys. Key management responsibilities belong to AWS KMS and customer processes.

options.text: Detecting underutilized resources to save costs

explanation.summary: AWS Trusted Advisor identifies underutilized resources to help reduce costs.
examples: Identifying idle EC2 instances
Detecting unattached EBS volumes
explanation.additionalInfo: Trusted Advisor continuously evaluates AWS environments against best practices. Cost optimization checks are a core feature and frequently appear in exam questions related to saving money and improving efficiency.

options.text: Improving security by proactively monitoring the AWS environment

explanation.summary: AWS Trusted Advisor provides proactive security recommendations.
keyPoints: Checks IAM and security group settings
Helps align with AWS best practices
examples: Detecting overly permissive security groups
Identifying IAM users without MFA
explanation.additionalInfo: Security checks are a major component of AWS Trusted Advisor. These checks help customers proactively identify and remediate security risks before they lead to incidents. This capability is commonly tested in AWS certification exams.

options.text: Implementing enforced tagging across AWS resources

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor does not enforce tagging policies.
explanation.why: Resource tagging enforcement is handled through AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies or AWS Config rules. Trusted Advisor may report missing tags but cannot enforce them.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage that users experience when they move on-premises workloads to the AWS Cloud?

options.text: Elimination of expenses for running and maintaining data centers

explanation.summary: Moving workloads to AWS eliminates the need to run and maintain on-premises data centers.
keyPoints: No need to purchase or maintain physical servers
Eliminates data center power and cooling costs
Removes expenses for physical security and facilities
Reduces staffing requirements for hardware maintenance
Shifts capital expenses to operational expenses
examples: Closing an on-premises data center after migrating workloads to AWS
Eliminating costs for hardware refresh cycles
Reducing IT staff effort spent on physical maintenance
explanation.additionalInfo: One of the core advantages of cloud computing is removing the burden of managing physical data centers. AWS customers no longer need to worry about server procurement, hardware failures, power outages, cooling systems, or facility security. These responsibilities are fully handled by AWS, allowing organizations to focus on application development and business value. This concept is central to AWS exams and aligns with the well-known benefit: 'Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers.'

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Six Advantages Of Cloud

options.text: Price discounts that are identical to discounts from hardware providers

explanation.summary: AWS pricing discounts are not identical to traditional hardware vendor discounts.
explanation.why: AWS pricing is based on consumption and economies of scale, not negotiated bulk hardware purchases. Discounts come from Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and usage-based reductions rather than vendor-style hardware pricing models.

options.text: Distribution of all operational controls to AWS

explanation.summary: Operational responsibility is shared, not fully transferred to AWS.
explanation.why: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS manages the infrastructure, but customers retain responsibility for applications, data, access control, and configurations. Operational control is not entirely handed over to AWS.

explanation.summary: Operational expenses are reduced but not eliminated when using AWS.
explanation.why: AWS shifts infrastructure costs to a pay-as-you-go model, but customers still incur operational expenses such as service usage, monitoring, security management, and application maintenance.

questions.question: A company wants to manage deployed IT services and govern its infrastructure as code (IaC) templates. Which AWS service will meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: AWS Resource Explorer is used to search and discover AWS resources, not to govern IaC templates.
explanation.why: Resource Explorer helps locate resources across regions and accounts but does not manage service catalogs or enforce governance over infrastructure templates.

explanation.summary: AWS Service Catalog enables governance and management of approved IT services and IaC templates.
keyPoints: Controls who can deploy which resources
examples: Providing approved EC2 and RDS templates to teams
Restricting deployment of non-compliant infrastructure
Standardizing environments across accounts
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Service Catalog allows organizations to define and manage a portfolio of approved CloudFormation templates. It ensures users can deploy only compliant infrastructure while maintaining flexibility through self-service. This service is commonly tested in exams when governance and IaC control are required.

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations manages accounts and policies, not IaC templates.
explanation.why: Organizations helps manage multiple AWS accounts and apply Service Control Policies, but it does not provide a catalog or governance for infrastructure templates.

explanation.summary: AWS Systems Manager focuses on operational management, not IaC governance.
explanation.why: Systems Manager provides tools for patching, automation, and operational visibility, but it does not manage or govern CloudFormation templates as a service catalog.

questions.question: Which AWS service or tool helps users visualize, understand, and manage spending and usage over time?

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations is used for account management, not cost visualization.
explanation.why: Organizations helps centrally manage multiple accounts and apply policies but does not provide detailed cost and usage visualizations.

explanation.summary: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates future costs but does not analyze historical usage.
explanation.why: The Pricing Calculator is used for forecasting costs before deployment. It does not visualize or manage actual spending and usage over time.

explanation.summary: AWS Cost Explorer provides detailed visualization and analysis of AWS spending and usage.
keyPoints: Visualizes historical cost and usage data
Supports filtering by service, account, and tags
Helps identify cost trends and anomalies
examples: Analyzing monthly EC2 spend trends
Identifying services driving cost increases
Tracking usage across linked accounts
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Cost Explorer is the primary tool for understanding and managing AWS costs over time. It allows customers to break down spending by service, region, account, and tags, making it essential for financial governance and cost optimization. This service is frequently tested in AWS certification exams.

learnMore.title: Aws Cost Management Aws Cost Explorer

explanation.summary: AWS Service Catalog governs deployments, not cost visualization.
explanation.why: Service Catalog controls which services and templates can be deployed but does not provide cost or usage analytics.

questions.question: A company is using a central data platform to manage multiple types of data for its customers. The company wants to use AWS services to discover, transform, and visualize the data. Which combination of AWS services should the company use to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

explanation.summary: AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service used to discover and transform data.
keyPoints: Integrates with Amazon S3 and analytics services
examples: Crawling data stored in Amazon S3 to build a data catalog
Transforming raw customer data into analytics-ready formats
Preparing datasets for visualization tools
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Glue is a core analytics service used to discover and transform data at scale. It automatically catalogs datasets, making them searchable and queryable by other analytics services. Glue jobs handle data cleansing, normalization, and transformation, which is essential before visualization. This service is commonly paired with Amazon QuickSight in exam scenarios involving data pipelines.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a file storage service and does not provide data transformation or visualization capabilities.
explanation.why: EFS is used for shared file storage across EC2 instances. It does not offer data discovery, ETL, or visualization features required for analytics workflows.

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse, but it is not required for discovery, transformation, and visualization in this scenario.
explanation.why: While Redshift can store and analyze data, the question specifically asks for discovering, transforming, and visualizing data. Glue and QuickSight directly address these needs without requiring a data warehouse.

explanation.summary: Amazon QuickSight is a serverless business intelligence service used to visualize data.
examples: Building dashboards to visualize customer behavior
Creating reports from transformed datasets
Sharing insights with business users
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon QuickSight is AWS’s primary visualization service. It connects directly to data sources prepared by AWS Glue and allows users to build interactive dashboards without managing infrastructure. In exams, QuickSight is the standard answer for data visualization requirements.

explanation.summary: Amazon QLDB is a ledger database and is not designed for analytics or visualization workflows.
explanation.why: QLDB is used for immutable transaction logs and audit trails. It does not provide ETL or visualization capabilities required for this use case.

questions.question: A global company wants to migrate its third-party applications to the AWS Cloud. The company wants help from a global team of experts to complete the migration faster and more reliably in accordance with AWS internal best practices. Which AWS service or resource will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS Support provides technical support but does not perform hands-on migrations.
explanation.why: AWS Support helps troubleshoot issues and answer questions but does not actively plan or execute migrations. Professional migration assistance requires a dedicated engagement service.

explanation.summary: AWS Professional Services provides expert guidance and hands-on assistance for cloud migrations.
examples: Migrating third-party enterprise applications
Designing migration strategies
Executing phased cloud adoption plans
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Professional Services works directly with customers to plan and execute cloud migrations using proven methodologies and AWS best practices. They provide architectural guidance, migration execution, and optimization. This option is commonly tested when expert-led migrations are required.

explanation.summary: AWS Launch Wizard automates deployment of specific workloads but does not provide migration expertise.
explanation.why: Launch Wizard helps deploy certain applications like SAP or Microsoft workloads but does not replace expert-led migration planning and execution.

explanation.summary: AWS Managed Services focuses on ongoing operations, not migration execution.
explanation.why: AMS helps operate and manage AWS environments after workloads are deployed. It does not primarily provide migration planning and execution services.
